checks.name: exact_target_preserved

evidence.reason: Original production draw/timer arming remains unchanged in the default path.
When r.random is nil, extra := time.Duration(rand.Int63()) % minVal and the timer is armed via r.clock.After; with realClock this is equivalent to time.After.
r.clock defaults to realClock when Config.Clock is nil, preserving wall-clock behavior.

checks.reason: Production defaults are preserved. util.go is byte-for-byte unchanged (randomTimeout still uses the global math/rand source), the no-controller branch of Raft.randomTimeoutFor is identical to the original draw, Config.Clock defaults to nil and NewRaft installs realClock (time.Now/time.After), and Config.Random defaults to nil. The pause gate fields are inert while unused (paused=false yields an immediate return from waitWhilePaused), so the target's public behavior is unchanged.

checks.name: existing_tests_unchanged

evidence.reason: Unchanged production helper means existing timing-sensitive tests keep their original behavior.
Existing test scaffolding is preserved and reused by the new tests.

checks.reason: No existing _test.go files were modified (patch_metrics lists only new test files), and the core changes are default-preserving/additive. Existing test helpers (inmemConfig, newTestLogger, MockFSM, MockFSM.Logs) remain available and the new tests compile against them.

checks.name: message_cache_injection_coherence

evidence.reason: Pending() calls copyPayload(e.payload) only; the separately buffered InstallSnapshot stream (pendingMessage.stream) is not copied into the returned PendingMessage.
pendingMessage carries stream []byte privately, but PendingMessage/MessagePayload expose no stream field.
The request entry is unlocked before target resolution and delivery, and removal occurs only after acceptance; a concurrent Inject of the same handle can deliver twice.
The stream is fully read into a private []byte at capture, confirming the stream is part of the captured message but is not surfaced in the public snapshot.

checks.reason: Two contract gaps remain in the shared capture/inject path. (1) The InstallSnapshot stream is buffered privately in pendingMessage.stream but never exposed by Pending(); Pending() returns only MessagePayload, so a controller-to-Pending deep snapshot omits the stream and the tester cannot inspect it (copy_safety requires deep snapshots including streams). (2) Inject() resolves and delivers outside the controller lock without first marking the entry as in-progress or removing it; two concurrent Inject calls on the same handle can both observe the entry in byHandle and both deliver before either removes it, producing duplicate delivery and violating thread-safety/no-duplication.

checks.name: original_send_suppressed

evidence.reason: Controlled branch calls t.controller.capture(...) and t.waitRPC(...); it never calls t.base.AppendEntries.
Controlled branch returns a controlledPipeline that captures each AppendEntries instead of opening the real pipeline.

checks.reason: In controlled mode every outbound Transport method (AppendEntries, RequestVote, RequestPreVote, InstallSnapshot, TimeoutNow, AppendEntriesPipeline) captures the request and blocks on the controller continuation without invoking the underlying InmemTransport send path; the real makeRPC enqueue occurs only on Inject. Responses re-enter through the controller's respCh watcher rather than the real transport response channel.

checks.name: protocol_logic_unchanged

evidence.reason: Nil Config.Clock installs realClock before goroutines start.
heartbeatTimer via randomTimeoutFor and r.clock.After/r.clock.Now preserve upstream timing in default mode.
Commit/heartbeat/backoff timers use r.clock/s.clock, defaulting to real time.

checks.reason: All core edits are default-disabled or semantically neutral in production mode. Timer arming, time checks, and lastContact writes route through r.clock/s.clock, which default to realClock; the no-controller random path is identical to the original; and the pause-gate select cases/poll are inert while never paused. No protocol, persistence, state-transition, or ordering change occurs in the default configuration.

checks.name: testing_contract_conformance

evidence.reason: Pause only flips the main-loop pause gate; it does not gate replication/FSM/snapshot goroutines.
replicate goroutine is started with goFunc and keeps running while the main leaderLoop is paused.
Launched with plain go, so Crash/Shutdown does not join it; it can still call r.trans.TimeoutNow after Crash returns.
Shared-clock advance has no per-node lifecycle awareness and does not skip paused/stopped/crashed nodes.

checks.reason: The common contract is not fully satisfied. LifecycleController.Pause gates only runFollower/runCandidate/leaderLoop; per-peer replication/heartbeat goroutines, runFSM, and runSnapshots keep running, so a paused node can still emit protocol output and progress time. Crash is Raft.Shutdown(), which joins only routinesGroup goroutines, leaving untracked plain-go goroutines (leadershipTransfer, emitLogStoreMetrics, transfer-timeout closures) able to emit protocol output after Crash returns. TimeController.Advance advances a shared virtual clock without excluding paused/stopped/crashed nodes, so paused-node timers still fire. These are implementation/contract mismatches, not mere risks.

issues.reason: Pause only blocks the three main protocol loops. Replication goroutines (replicate/heartbeat in replication.go), runFSM, and runSnapshots are not gated, so a paused node can still send heartbeats/AppendEntries (protocol output) and advance node time. This violates the pause_resume contract ('prevents message handling, node time progress, and protocol output').

Crash is implemented as Raft.Shutdown(), which waits only for routinesGroup (goFunc) goroutines. leadershipTransfer (raft.go:813, plain go), emitLogStoreMetrics (raft.go:522, plain go), and the transfer-timeout closures are untracked, so after Crash returns an in-flight leadership transfer can still emit TimeoutNow protocol output. This violates the crash contract ('no abandoned execution context may process protocol work, emit output...').

Advance drives one shared virtual clock with no node-state awareness. Paused nodes' armed timers still fire into buffered channels (and replication goroutines continue to consume steps), violating v0_scope ('Paused, stopped, and crashed nodes do not receive steps').

The InstallSnapshot stream is buffered privately (pendingMessage.stream) but Pending() returns only MessagePayload, omitting the stream. Pending therefore does not return a complete deep snapshot including streams as required by copy_safety.

Inject delivers outside the controller lock without marking the entry in-progress or removing it before delivery. Two concurrent Inject calls on the same handle can both resolve and deliver the message before either removes it, causing duplicate delivery and violating thread-safety and the no-duplication rule.

risks: Transport-level RPC send/wait timeouts (ControlledTransport.waitRPC and MessageController.Inject send) remain wall-clock based; combining TimeController with long real-time gaps between Inject(request) and Inject(response) can produce spurious 'command timed out' results. This is disclosed as an RPC-delivery-deadline exclusion, not a protocol timer.

LifecycleController.Register captures a value copy of Config; Clock and Random controller references are preserved across Restart, but post-registration Config mutations are not propagated until re-registration.

TimeController.nodes is bookkeeping-only and is not automatically re-bound on LifecycleController.Restart; behavior is unaffected because Advance is clock-driven and the fresh runtime inherits Config.Clock/Config.Random.
